Actually, maybe just do a search online for a guy named Arieh Smith (a.k.a. "Xiao Mei"). He was the one I learned this from. I could not care less which is true or whoever thinks it is true.

replies.author: @bryansiew9707
replies.text:
Fujianese is not a subset of Mandarin, if you’re referring to 闽语. 
Fujianese is sometimes seen as a Chinese dialect because the written version of it can be understood by other Chinese languages speakers, e.g. Mandarin speaker, to some extend. But this doesn’t make Fujianese a dialect of Mandarin, both of them are dialects of “Chinese” under this definition.
Some wouldn’t call it dialect because the spoken version of it cannot be understood by other Chinese speakers. That’s just a special thing caused by the Chinese writing system, which is basically just an ancient emoji that doesn’t carry the sound.
